summary:
Allocate `k` slots once and keep two numbers: `head` (where the front item is) and `size`. The back slot is
`(head + size − 1) mod k` and the next free slot is `(head + size) mod k`, so indices wrap around the end of
the array. Enqueue writes a slot, dequeue advances `head`: nothing ever shifts, and every operation is O(1).

question.md:
Implement a bounded FIFO buffer of capacity `k` with `enqueue`, `dequeue`, `front`, `rear`, `isEmpty` and
`isFull`. Failed operations report `false` (or −1 for reading an empty buffer) and change nothing.

- **Full and empty must be told apart**, even though in both cases the front and back 'meet' in a circular
  layout.
- **`rear` is the most recently added item still in the buffer.**
- **Up to 10⁵ calls with `k ≤ 1000`.**

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Enqueue on a full buffer fails and changes nothing; dequeue on an empty one fails.
- `front`/`rear` return −1 when empty.
- Capacity 1: front and rear are the same slot.

think.md:
**Wrap around instead of shifting.** A plain list that removes from the front shifts every item: O(n) per
dequeue. A fixed array of size `k` with a `head` index and a `size` avoids that: the front is `buf[head]`, the
next free slot is `(head + size) mod k`, and dequeuing just moves `head` forward. When an index passes the end,
`mod k` wraps it to the start, so the array behaves like a ring.

**Why store `size` rather than a tail index.** With only `head` and `tail`, an empty buffer and a full one look
the same (`head == tail`); the size tells them apart.

approaches.title: List with shifting

idea.md: Use a list: append to enqueue, remove index 0 to dequeue, and check the length against `k`.

build: Length checks for full and empty.

lines.text: Items in queue order, and the capacity.
Refuse when full; otherwise append at the back.
Refuse when empty; otherwise remove the front, which shifts every remaining item one place left.
Front and back are the ends of the list; −1 when empty.
Empty and full come straight from the length.

steps.text: enqueue(1): added at the back → true.
enqueue(2): added at the back → true.
enqueue(3): added at the back → true.
enqueue(4): full → false.
rear(): 3.
isFull(): true.
dequeue(): remove the front and shift the other 2 item(s) left → true.
enqueue(4): added at the back → true.
rear(): 4.
front(): 2.
Every dequeue shifted the whole list.

walk.title: A list that grows at the back and shifts everything left when the front leaves. Capacity 3.

limits.md: Removing from the front shifts every item. A ring buffer moves an index instead.

approaches.title: Fixed array, head index and size

idea.md: Fixed array of size `k`, `head` and `size`. Enqueue writes at `(head + size) mod k`; dequeue advances `head`; rear is at `(head + size − 1) mod k`.

lines.text: `k` slots allocated once; `head` = slot of the front item; `size` = items stored.
Full → refuse. Otherwise the first free slot is `size` steps after `head`, wrapping with `% k`.
Empty → refuse. Otherwise the front slot is simply abandoned: advance `head` (wrapping) and shrink `size`. No data moves.
The last stored item is `size − 1` steps after `head`, wrapping. (`head + size − 1` is never negative when `size ≥ 1`.)
Counting items makes empty (`0`) and full (`k`) unambiguous, which a head/tail pair alone can't do.

steps.text: enqueue(1): write slot (head + size) mod k = 0; size 1 → true.
enqueue(2): write slot (head + size) mod k = 1; size 2 → true.
enqueue(3): write slot (head + size) mod k = 2; size 3 → true.
enqueue(4): size = 3 = capacity → false.
rear(): slot (head + size − 1) mod k = 2 → 3.
isFull(): size 3 == 3 → true.
dequeue(): just advance head to 1 (nothing moves); size 2 → true.
enqueue(4): write slot (head + size) mod k = 0; size 3 → true.
rear(): slot (head + size − 1) mod k = 0 → 4.
front(): slot 1 → 2.
Every operation is O(1): the data never moves, only the head index and the count change.

walk.title: A fixed array of 3 slots, the index of the front item, and the count. The back is at (head + size − 1) mod k; indices wrap around.

takeaways.md:
- **Circular queue:** fixed array, `head` and `size`, indices taken `mod k`.
- Track the size to tell full from empty.
- **Pitfall:** computing the rear as `head + size` (one past the last item).
